subject: Private deployment: license carveouts, audit window & evidence access
messages:
From: Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@stellatherapeutics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: CFO - Stella Therapeutics <cfo@stellatherapeutics.com>
Date: 2026-08-19T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment: license carveouts, audit window & evidence access

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the demo last week. We are preparing the procurement packet for our Security & IT review. Two asks from our legal and infrastructure teams before we route to finance: 

1) License boundary: we need written confirmation that a private (VPC) deployment license limits runtime rights to our named instance/region only and does not grant any replication or derivative rights outside the order form scope.

2) Audit & evidence: Stella requires an evidence matrix and a temporary audit window (2 business days) where our internal auditors can run a read-only witness of runtime logs and a snapshot handoff. We'd like clarity on what artifacts Redwood can commit to — snapshots, runbooks, operator witness, and whether a sealed escrow-style transfer is possible for agentless validation.

3) KMS & key custody: we need to confirm whether Redwood supports customer KMS integration (Azure Key Vault) for tenant-encrypted secrets in the private deployment, and what handback looks like on termination.

Attached is our draft order form and a short evidence checklist (ST_OrderForm_ScopedAddendum.pdf). Can you confirm what your legal team needs in order to produce a redline? Time is tight — aim to get this to procurement legal by EOD Friday if possible.

Appreciate it,
Sam Ortega
Head of Procurement
Stella Therapeutics

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@stellatherapeutics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-19T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: license carveouts, audit window & evidence access

Sam —

Thanks for the clear list. We can move fast on this. Quick summary / next steps from our side: 

- License boundary: we will produce a short MSA addendum language that explicitly limits licensed runtime to the customer environment described in the order form and prohibits derivative redistribution. This will be a narrow "deployment-only" grant with standard carveouts for debugging and compliance.

- Audit & evidence: we can offer a staged evidence package: (A) pre-signed sealed snapshot (hash + encrypted bundle retained by us), (B) operator-witness session (Redwood engineer + customer auditor) for up to 2 business days, and (C) a documented runbook + sample logs redaction. We need to confirm whether Stella requires physical site witnessing or a remote witness is sufficient.

- KMS & key custody: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS integrations for private deploys. We can integrate with Azure Key Vault; on termination we provide a documented key-handback procedure. If Stella wants HSM-bounded transfer or escrowed key escrow, that'll require legal review and an exhibit.

I looped in Marissa (our Contracts lead) and David (Platform ops) to draft the redline and evidence matrix. I'll follow up with a short call window; are you available 1:00–1:30pm PT today to align?

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-19T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Private deployment: license carveouts, audit window & evidence access

Jordan / David —

I reviewed Sam's asks and sketched a redline. Key points in the attached doc (MSA_Redline_v3.docx) and the evidence spreadsheet (evidence_matrix.xlsx):

- License grant: proposed narrow language under Section 2.1: "Customer is granted a non-transferable, non-sublicensable license to run the licensed runtime within the Customer Designated Environment as specified in the Order Form. Any replication, redistribution, or derivative redistribution outside the Order Form scope is prohibited."

- For clarity I added an exhibit (Exhibit E) that enumerates permitted artifacts and the maximum audit window (48 hours) with scope. Exhibit language includes the phrase "witness-only" to restrict tooling access to read-only operations and explicit redaction rules for customer-sensitive PII.

- Escrow-like option: included two options in Exhibit F — (1) sealed snapshot deposit with dual-key encryption (Redwood holds hash only) and (2) trusted third-party witness (recommended for regulated customers). Both are conditional on mutual NDAs and limited liability carveouts.

- KMS handback: added a runbook reference requiring customer-side KMS keys to be injected at deploy time; on termination we will perform a documented key export or zeroization depending on key lifecycle. That will be surfaced as an Order Form checkbox ("Customer-managed KMS: yes/no").

Open items for legal / ops confirmation:
1) Can Platform deliver a read-only operator witness without privileged shell access? David — please confirm the exact artifacts we can expose and how logs will be redacted.
2) For Option (1) sealed snapshot: ops needs guidance on encryption key escrow (dual-control) and retention period.

I'll upload the redline and evidence matrix to the deal folder once I tidy comments. Priyom, please review liability language — we may need to limit indemnity related to third-party audits.

Marissa Cole
Head of Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MSA_Redline_v3.docx (docx), evidence_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@stellatherapeutics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: CFO - Stella Therapeutics <cfo@stellatherapeutics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: license carveouts, audit window & evidence access

Jordan / Marissa / David —

Thanks, that all looks sensible. A couple quick clarifications from our security team: 

- Remote witness is acceptable; physical sight is not required. Please ensure operator-witness sessions are recorded and that recordings are retained for 90 days for auditability.
- For sealed snapshot option, Stella prefers the dual-key escrow route with the TTP held by our legal counsel. We'll send contact details for the trustee once NDA is executed.
- KMS: Azure Key Vault integration is a must. Please confirm whether there will be any managed-service keys held by Redwood as part of deployment (we prefer Redwood never hold private key material).

If you can incorporate those clarifications in the redline and share an updated package (MSA + Exhibit E/F + evidence spreadsheet), we will route immediately to procurement legal and aim to sign prior to month-end.

Appreciate the turnaround.

—Sam
